title: DeepMind's own numbers say the opposite happened.
description:
DeepMind's own numbers say the opposite happened. It searched far less of the board, not more.

DeepMind trained it on nothing but chess's rules and self-play, no opening books, no human games, no hand-built evaluation function.

Starting from random play, AlphaZero was already outplaying Stockfish, 2016's reigning world-champion engine, after 4 hours of training. 300,000 self-play steps, and it had already caught up.

What AlphaZero actually searches per second in chess, against Stockfish's 70 million a second. It won by searching less, not more.

A 100-game match at tournament time controls: 28 wins, 72 draws, 0 losses, for AlphaZero. Beaten on selectivity, not on speed.
